note_en: Commissioning year 2016: Inox Wind announced on 2 March 2016 a turnkey order from PTC Energy for a 20 MW project at Nipaniya, Mandsaur district, Madhya Pradesh, due by March 2016; in April 2017 PTC Energy said it already had 50 MW operating in Madhya Pradesh and that its new total of 288.8 MW was nearly six times its capacity at the start of fiscal 2016–17 (April 2016), i.e. about 50 MW then. Besides the 30 MW Jaora farm commissioned on 8 March 2016, that leaves Nipaniya’s 20 MW operating by the end of March 2016
why: The year is derived, not stated in one sentence: (1) the 10 × 2 MW Inox order was announced on 2 Mar 2016, so it was not built before March 2016; (2) by April 2017 PTC Energy had 50 MW operating in MP, which can only be Jaora (30 MW, 8 Mar 2016) + Nipaniya (20 MW); (3) 288.8 MW being 'nearly 6 times' the capacity at the start of FY2016-17 means about 50 MW on 1 Apr 2016 (with only Jaora it would be ~9.6 times). So Nipaniya was commissioned in March 2016. If the caller treats this arithmetic as too indirect, downgrade to lead (year 2016 or early 2017). Owner: PTC Energy Ltd (100% PTC India subsidiary at the time).

note_zh: 同一座風場：IFC 揭露文件所述 Bhilwara Energy 在拉賈斯坦邦賈沙梅爾的 20 MW 集團自用風電專案位於 Pokaran 區 Rajgarh 與 Bhaisara 村、Inox Renewables 的 300 MW 風場內，專案文件放在 Dangri 村的 Inox 匯流變電所；這筆 20 MW 與「Jaisalmer (Bhilwara)」（20 MW，2013 年）是同一案，重複計算
note_en: Same farm: IFC’s disclosure describes Bhilwara Energy’s 20 MW group-captive wind project in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, at the villages of Rajgarh and Bhaisara (Pokaran tehsil) inside Inox Renewables’ 300 MW wind farm, with its documents kept at Inox’s pooling substation in Dangri village; this 20 MW record and “Jaisalmer (Bhilwara)” (20 MW, 2013) are the same project counted twice
why: Both GEM records are 20 MW, owner 'Bhilwara Energy Ltd [100%]', in Jaisalmer district, ~36 km apart; 'Jaisalmer (Bhilwara)' (src G, year 2013) cites the CEA list and this IFC disclosure, while 'Dangri (Bhilwara)' cites BEL's old about-us page. The IFC summary lists BEL's other assets (Malana 86 MW, AD Hydro 192 MW, Bhilwara Green Energy 49.5 MW wind in Maharashtra) and only this one wind project in Rajasthan. Commissioning was 'expected by March 31, 2013' (expected, so the kept record's 2013 is GEM's own). If the caller wants stronger proof that BEL never had a second 20 MW Jaisalmer farm, treat as lead. BEL's current site lists only 14 MW at Bhendwade (Kolhapur), so the Jaisalmer project appears to have been sold since. Side note (not on this list): 'Satara (Bhilwara)' and 'Kukudwad' (both 50 MW, 2012, Bhilwara group) look like another possible duplicate pair.
